verdict: Accepted on attempt 1, no retry. Both turns complete (474.8 s and 424.9 s), 246 tool calls, 9 failed, 3 restart cards answered with real Core restarts and nothing else. Post-run real browser, measured rather than asserted: connecting the last visible candidate grew the slots 3 -> 4 and disconnecting it trimmed them back 4 -> 3, read from the live node's own inputs array; selector 1 executed [5,1,2,5,6] and returned N2-A with the B branch unevaluated, selector 2 executed [5,3,4,5,6] and returned N3-B with A unevaluated, and branch_served_from_cache is empty on every queue so the cache-nonce guard held; selector 99 raised the bounded SelectionError 'selector 99 is out of range 1..32; connected slots [1,2]' with ZERO branches executed and no engine IndexError/KeyError/TypeError -- which is exactly the failure demofarm-3's enabled arm shipped. Turn 2 added fallback_to_first_connected: with the flag false a disconnected slot 2 kept the bounded diagnostic and ran nothing, with it true the node chose the lowest connected input and executed only [5,1,2,5,6] -> N6-A, and save plus full reload preserved select=1, the flag=true and the widget order [select, fallback_to_first_connected].
evidence_gaps: Neither arm drove a browser, and both said so: /health reports shell disabled with reason 'no sandbox mechanism on this platform'. Every interaction, laziness and persistence measurement is post-run operator scoring against each arm's own Core, run strictly sequentially. No screen recording was made.

local_valid is FAIL on all four scored packages, on both arms, and the single finding is identical: LOCAL-005 'no stable node id could be statically extracted from the package'. This is a static-analysis false positive, not a package defect -- validator.py:341 accepts node_id only as an ast.Constant, and both arms wrote node_id=NODE_ID with a module-level constant. The dynamic evidence contradicts it on every package: exactly one class, byte-identical before and after a real restart, collision-free against the frozen baseline. It is a rubric item, so it is reported as failed on both arms rather than excused; the gap is symmetric and does not bias the comparison. Recorded as R-596. Do NOT compare this against demofarm-21's and demofarm-22's 'validator 0 errors' as a quality regression -- those pairs wrote the id inline and so did not trip the same limitation.
cloud_compatible is fail on both arms and is not a rubric item, as in demofarm-21 and -22.
